name: Retail and e-commerce
purpose: customer service, complaints and refunds, payments and fraud, age-restricted sales, shoplifting and conflict, slips and spills, manual handling, deliveries and click and collect, accessibility

identity.place: A neighbourhood supermarket of about 1,000 m2 of sales floor on a suburban high street in a temperate town: a single-storey 1990s building of buff brick and grey profiled metal cladding, its glazed shopfront facing the street, a customer car park at the side and a service yard behind. Inside, one open sales floor: a bank of staffed checkouts and self-checkouts across the front, the customer service desk beside the entrance, aisles of low gondolas running from front to back, chilled cabinets along the back wall, and behind that wall the stockroom and goods-in. An ordinary, well-run, busy shop, not a showroom.
architecture: an exposed roof: white-painted steel portal frames about 6 m apart with purlins and the white underside of the profiled roof deck, 5.0 m high at the walls and about 6.0 m at the ridge; long rows of linear LED lights hung on white trunking at 3.6 m, one row over each aisle
walls of white-painted blockwork (the block courses faintly visible); above the chillers and the wall shelving the walls are plain white to the eaves, with a long blank sign band at 4.0 to 4.5 m
a floor of pale grey speckled non-slip ceramic tiles 0.6 m square with thin grey grout lines; in the stockroom, sealed grey concrete with yellow painted walkway lines

mid-floor gondolas only 1.6 m high, so staff can see across the floor: white steel uprights and back panels in 1.25 m bays, a solid base deck, four shelves with grey shelf-edge price strips; wall shelving 2.0 m high along the side walls; open-fronted chilled cabinets 1.95 m high along the back wall

the shopfront: aluminium-framed glazing in dark grey frames from 0.6 m to 3.0 m above a low buff brick upstand across most of the front, with a pair of automatic sliding doors and a dark entrance mat inside them; at the left end a solid pier 1.5 m wide, and at the right end a solid stretch of front wall behind the customer service desk (the cash office is beyond it); inside, these solid parts are white-painted blockwork like the other walls

doors: a pair of grey steel swing doors with round vision panels and stainless kick plates in the back wall to the stockroom; fire exits as single steel doors with a horizontal push bar, a green exit sign above each
identity.materials: white-painted blockwork and steel, pale grey speckled floor tiles, white powder-coated gondola steel with grey shelf-edge strips, the store's colour (a deep cobalt blue) on the checkout and service desk fronts and the gondola end caps' header panels, light oak-effect laminate on counter tops, brushed stainless steel in the bagging areas, grey concrete and galvanised steel shelving in the stockroom; signal colours only where they are in life: yellow wet-floor signs and walkway lines, red fire extinguishers and call points, green exit signs
inhabited: trade in progress: a cardboard tray of tins half put out on a shelf, a price gun left on a shelf edge, a gap where a line has sold out, a flattened box waiting to go to the baler
customers' traces: a basket left on the floor by a chiller, a receipt on the floor by the tills, a trolley parked at the end of an aisle
the shop's working kit: a yellow wet-floor sign folded against a wall, a handheld scanner on a lanyard, a safety step stool, carrier bags on their hooks
slight wear: scuffed kick plates on the stockroom doors, a chipped gondola base, a worn grey path in the tiles at the entrance
scale: a person is about 1.75 m tall; the walls rise to 5.0 m (nearly three people high); doors are 2.1 m high
gondolas are 1.6 m high and about 1.1 m deep back to back, in 1.25 m bays; aisles between them about 2.0 m; the cross aisles at the front and back about 3 m; wall shelving 2.0 m; chillers 1.95 m

a checkout counter and belt are about 0.9 m high, 0.8 m wide and 4.5 m long; the cashier sits at about 0.65 m on a high swivel seat; a checkout lane is about 1.0 m wide; the card terminal sits on a swivel stand at about 1.1 m
the customer service desk: a standing counter at about 1.05 m with a lowered section at about 0.8 m

the stockroom: steel longspan shelving 2.4 m high in 2.0 m bays, 0.6 m deep; roll cages about 0.8 m by 0.7 m and 1.8 m high; a pallet 1.2 by 1.0 m; the goods-in roller shutter about 3.0 m wide and 3.5 m high
a wet-floor sign is an A-frame about 0.6 m high; a fire extinguisher hangs with its handle about 1.0 m up; exit signs sit 2.2 to 2.4 m up above the doors
identity.default_light: A bright, overcast late morning outside. Inside, the sales floor is lit by the long rows of linear LED lights over the aisles: a clean, even, neutral white from above with soft shadows falling almost straight down; the chilled cabinets glow with their own cool white lights; near the shopfront, soft grey daylight from the glazing adds a cooler light from the front. The stockroom has plainer strip lights and grey daylight from the goods-in shutter when it is open.
identity.outside: Through the shopfront: a wide pavement with a bin and a bench, parked cars, the brick terraces and shopfronts of the high street opposite (no names, no signs, no logos), a pale overcast sky.
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene so the sets belong to one shop (each scene names the ones its camera can see): the white steel portal frames and roof deck with the rows of linear LED lights, the pale grey speckled floor tiles, the deep cobalt blue of the counters and end-cap headers, the low white 1.6 m gondolas with grey shelf-edge strips, white-painted blockwork, a yellow safety element (a wet-floor sign or a walkway line), a green exit sign.
avoid: real brands, logos, product names, readable prices, signs or packaging with words; products are plain packs in soft colours with blank labels
people in the sets (the cast is separate)
a showroom-clean shop: every scene shows trade happening
stock or boxes on top of the gondolas, above head height on wall shelving, or blocking an aisle, a fire exit or a fire extinguisher
anything that pins a country (flags, currency symbols, number plates); notes and coins are plain shapes
weapons, blood or anything frightening; a shoplifting or conflict scene is shown by the cast, not by the set

cast.role: customer assistants of varied ages and backgrounds (navy polo shirt, a deep cobalt fleece or tabard, a plain name badge, a handheld scanner on a lanyard)
the store manager and shift leaders (smart shirt or blouse, a lanyard, a radio clipped to the belt)
stockroom and night-shift colleagues (navy work trousers and polo, safety shoes, rigger gloves; hi-vis vest in the yard)
customers of all ages and backgrounds (C15 brief), some with a basket, a trolley, a buggy, a walking stick or a wheelchair
a store security officer (dark uniform, plain badge, radio)
delivery drivers (hi-vis vest, a handheld scanner)

research: Real-world facts checked on 2026-10-15 (slips, spills and wet-floor signs: HSE retail slips and trips page; roll cages and pushing: HSE roll cage guidance; aisle widths: a retail design article; gondola heights and depths: a commissary specification and fixture makers' pages, sizes only; checkout and card terminal sizes: makers' pages, sizes only; seated checkout work: HSE INDG269 summary; counter heights: a UK building-control decision; security pedestals: makers' pages, sizes only; age checks: UK licensing conditions; longspan shelving: makers' pages; fire exits and stockrooms: fire safety guidance summaries). Sources, the scene choice (D-156) and what was not verified: docs/research/2026-10-13-sets-retail.md.

objects.gondola shelving: a run of mid-floor shelving units in 1.25 m bays, 1.6 m high: white steel uprights with slotted fronts, a solid back panel down the middle (the run is double-sided, about 1.1 m deep overall), a solid base deck about 0.15 m high on a kick plate, and four flat shelves above it about 0.4 m deep, each with a grey shelf-edge price strip along its front; every bay is full of plain packs except where the scene says
objects.plain product packs: rows of products with no words or logos: tins with plain paper bands in soft colours, cereal-style boxes in pale tints, bottles and jars with blank labels, packets standing upright; each line in a neat block a facing or two deep, fronts pulled forward to the shelf edge
objects.shelf-edge strip: a grey plastic strip about 40 mm tall along every shelf front holding small blank white price labels at each product line (slots, no numbers)
objects.chilled cabinets: open-fronted multideck chilled cabinets 1.95 m high in a long run: a white steel body with a canopy along the top holding a strip light, four or five sloping shelves lit from above, a low front lip, a dark night blind rolled up under the canopy, small grilles at the base; inside, plain cartons and packs in soft colours
objects.roof and lights: the exposed roof seen from below: white steel portal frame rafters every 6 m, lighter purlins across them and the white ribbed underside of the roof deck, high above; long straight rows of linear LED light fittings, each a slim white body about 60 mm wide with an opal diffuser, hung end to end from white trunking on short wires at 3.6 m
objects.sign band: a long plain panel on the wall at 4.0 to 4.5 m, painted deep cobalt blue with a thin white edge, left blank (a slot for words that are never drawn)
objects.cardboard tray of stock: a shallow brown cardboard tray about 0.4 by 0.3 m holding a dozen plain tins, its shrink-wrap cut and peeled back, standing on the floor at the foot of a shelf
objects.price gun: a small grey plastic hand labeller with a pistol grip, a trigger and a roll of blank labels, lying on a shelf edge
objects.shopping basket: a hand basket about 0.45 m long and 0.3 m wide in plain grey plastic with a grid of slots, two folding handles, standing on the floor
objects.wet-floor sign: a bright yellow plastic A-frame about 0.6 m high with a handle slot at the top and a plain black warning pictogram of a figure slipping (no words) on each face
objects.checkout: a staffed checkout: a counter about 4.5 m long and 0.9 m high with a deep cobalt blue front and a light oak-effect top; at the shop end a black rubber belt about 0.4 m wide with a plain divider bar resting on it, in the middle a glass flatbed scanner set flush in the top and a small weighing plate, then a brushed stainless bagging well with a sloping shelf and carrier bag hooks; the cashier sits in a pod beside the scanner on a high seat, behind a low side panel, with the cash drawer under the counter and the till screen on a short pole facing the cashier
objects.card terminal: a hand-sized card payment terminal in dark grey on a swivel stand at the lane edge of the counter, its keypad plain squares and its small screen a slot, turned toward the customer
objects.customer display: a small flat screen about 0.25 m wide on a short grey pole at the counter's lane edge, turned toward the customer; its face a slot
objects.cashier seat: a high swivel stool with a padded seat about 0.65 m high, a short curved backrest, a round footring and a five-spoke base on glides
objects.carrier bags: plain reusable bags in pale colours hanging from a bar of hooks at the bagging end, and a stack of folded paper bags in a holder (no logos)
objects.shopfront glazing: aluminium-framed glazing in dark grey frames from 0.6 m to 3.0 m, panes about 1.5 m wide above a low buff brick upstand, the glass showing the pavement, parked cars and the high street opposite in soft daylight, never a blank white
objects.service desk: a customer service desk in two heights: a standing counter at 1.05 m with a light oak-effect top and a deep cobalt blue front, and a lowered section at 0.8 m with knee space on the public side; behind it a staff work surface with drawers, a desk screen on a short pole facing the staff, a receipt printer, a card terminal on a swivel stand at the lowered section
objects.parcel shelving: one bay of grey steel shelving about 1.1 m wide, 0.5 m deep and 2.0 m high with four shelves of click and collect parcels: plain brown boxes and grey plastic bags of different sizes, each with a white label (a slot, no writing), set on the floor against the wall behind the desk's end
objects.EAS pedestals: a pair of slim security gate pedestals at the entrance, each about 1.6 m high, 0.4 m wide and 0.05 m thick: a clear acrylic panel in a pale grey frame on a small grey base screwed to the floor, a thin strip light along the top; about 2.0 m apart either side of the doorway
objects.sliding entrance doors: a pair of automatic sliding glass doors about 2.0 m wide and 2.1 m high in dark grey aluminium frames, a sensor box over the middle, set into the glazed shopfront; inside them a dark grey entrance mat 2 m deep set flush in the floor
objects.basket stand: a stack of a dozen grey plastic shopping baskets on a low grey stand about 0.75 m high, their handles folded down
objects.returned item: a plain white box the size of a kettle box, its flaps open, standing on the desk
objects.longspan shelving: galvanised and blue-grey steel longspan shelving 2.4 m high in 2.0 m bays, 0.6 m deep: slotted upright frames with diagonal bracing, orange-brown step beams, chipboard decks on four levels, loaded with plain brown cardboard cases (no words), heavier cases on the lower levels; a blank white label on each beam (slot)
objects.roll cage: a steel mesh roll container about 0.8 m long, 0.7 m wide and 1.8 m high: a galvanised wire-mesh frame with three high sides and an open front with two webbing straps across it, a mesh base on four 125 mm castors, a push handle at about 1.0 m on one end; loaded with plain cardboard cases stacked below head height, heavier ones at the bottom
objects.pallet and pallet truck: a timber pallet 1.2 by 1.0 m and 0.15 m high stacked with plain brown cases to about 1.2 m, wrapped in clear stretch film partly cut away; under it the forks of a hand pallet truck with a long steel tow handle on a hydraulic pump unit, its two load wheels at the fork tips, the handle standing upright toward us
objects.cardboard baler: a vertical cardboard baler about 1.0 m wide, 0.8 m deep and 2.4 m high: a pale grey steel cabinet with a hinged mesh loading gate at the front, a lower bale door with a heavy handle, a small control box with two round buttons and a red stop button on its side, a plain yellow and black hazard band along the gate, a few flattened boxes leaning beside it
objects.roller shutter: a goods-in roller shutter about 3.0 m wide and 3.5 m high: horizontal ribbed galvanised steel slats in vertical side guides, a box housing at the top, a bottom rail with a rubber seal, a grey push-button control box on the wall beside it; closed in the main set
objects.fire exit door: a single steel fire exit door about 1.0 m wide and 2.1 m high, painted light grey, a horizontal push bar across it at about 1.0 m, a closer at the top, a green exit sign (running figure, door and arrow, no words) above it, a 1.0 m wide keep-clear area hatched in yellow on the floor in front of it
objects.fire extinguisher: a red cylinder about 0.5 m tall with a black hose and a squeeze handle, on a wall bracket with its handle at about 1.0 m, a small blank plate above it
objects.walkway lines: yellow lines about 0.1 m wide painted on the grey concrete floor: the keep-clear hatching in front of the fire exit and a marked pedestrian route along the stockroom
objects.strip lights and roof lights: the stockroom's roof seen from below: the same white portal frames and purlins, a few translucent roof panels between them letting in soft daylight, and rows of plain linear LED battens hung at 3.2 m

scenes.what: an aisle of the supermarket's sales floor: two runs of low white gondolas full of plain packs on either side, receding to the back cross aisle, the chilled cabinets glowing along the back wall and plain white wall above them to the roof
scenes.for: the shop floor: helping a customer, spills and slips, spotting concealment and shoplifting, replenishment and safe lifting, accessibility and reaching, lone and late working
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs across the aisle (its centre line at x 0); y runs from the front cross aisle by the tills (the camera's side) to the back wall (y 16.0). The walls rise to 5.0 m; the roof's portal frames are above.

The aisle: 2.0 m wide between two gondola runs whose shelf faces are at x -1.0 and x 1.0, each 1.6 m high, running from y 0 to y 12.0 in 1.25 m bays. The first bay of each run (y 0 to 1.25) is close to the camera at the frame's edges.

At y 12.0 both runs end in end caps facing the back cross aisle (3.1 m wide, y 12.0 to 15.1). Along the back wall, the chilled cabinets, 1.95 m high, from y 15.1 to 16.0. Above them the back wall is plain white blockwork to the eaves at 5.0 m, with a blank sign band from 4.0 to 4.5 m (x -3.5 to 3.5).
A row of linear LED lights hangs at 3.6 m along the aisle's centre line; other rows hang over the neighbouring aisles.
On the floor: a cardboard tray of tins at the foot of the right run, x 0.85, y 2.7; a shopping basket left by the chillers at x 0.3, y 14.7.
Cast: a customer assistant standing at the right run, replenishing (x 0.6, y 2.3, head top 1.72 m); a customer with a basket standing at the left run (x -0.5, y 2.6, head top 1.66 m).

Camera: x 0, y -1.5 (in the front cross aisle, at the aisle's mouth), eye height 1.15 m (a low camera, so heads are seen against the plain wall above the chillers, not the shelves), looking straight along the aisle; 35 mm lens (55 degrees across); no tilt; horizon at 52 percent.

scenes.composition: A strong one-point view. The two gondola runs fill the left and right edges and recede to the back cross aisle: the left run's top edge falls from the top-left corner to its end at x 823, y 500 (its foot at y 719), the right run's from the top-right corner to x 1097, y 500 (foot y 719); the first bays end at x 289 (left) and x 1631 (right), their tops at y 260, their feet below the frame. Between the runs the tiled floor narrows to the far end. Beyond the end caps (outer edges x 673 and 1247) the back cross aisle, then the chilled cabinets glowing along the back wall (x 627 to 1293 visible, top y 467, foot y 689) with a basket on the floor in front of them (x 994, y 693). Above them the plain white back wall rises to the eaves (y 156), the blank sign band across it (x 591 to 1329, y 209 to 261); the aisle's light row comes down the centre from the top edge to y 270. The tray of tins sits at the right run's foot (x 1333, y 957). Free zones for the cast: (1) the customer assistant at the right run, turned to the shelf or toward the customer, seen full length (head top x 1251, y 285; feet x 1251, y 1120, just below the frame); her shelf at about x 1445, y 586; (2) the customer at the left run, seen full length (head top x 735, y 332; feet x 735, y 1079); the shelf beside her at about x 510, y 584. Both heads are seen against the plain white back wall above the chillers (the assistant's at x 2.76 on the wall, 2.67 to 3.78 m up; the customer's at x -2.13, 2.3 to 3.33 m up, above the chillers' 1.95 m tops and below the sign band): the low camera sees over the 1.6 m gondola tops behind them. Keep the gondola tops' edges just under the chins, never across a face.
scenes.light: Late morning. The key light is the aisle's row of linear LED lights directly above the centre line: a clean neutral white from above, so the shelf faces are lit evenly, each shelf edge throws a thin shadow onto the packs just below it, the gondola bases sit in soft shade, and the cast's and the tray's shadows fall almost straight down onto the tiles. The chilled cabinets at the far end glow a cooler white from their canopy lights and are the brightest band in the frame; the back wall above them is lit softly from the light rows. A little cool daylight from the shopfront behind the camera touches the floor at the bottom edge. The aisle is about 17 m deep: haze 0.1 at the far wall.
scenes.far: The shell and everything behind the cast: the roof and its light rows, the back wall with the sign band, the chilled cabinets, the back cross aisle with the end caps and the basket, the floor, and both gondola runs from the second bay onward (y 1.25 to 12.0) with all their packs and shelf-edge strips.
scenes.mid: Only the cardboard tray of tins on the floor at the right run's foot, in front of the assistant's feet.
scenes.near: The first bay of each gondola run (y 0 to 1.25), cropped by the left and right edges and the top and bottom: on the left from the edge to x 289, on the right from x 1631 to the edge; full of plain packs; they cover no cast zone.

scenes.what: the end checkout of the supermarket's bank of staffed tills, beside the plain white side wall near the shopfront: a long cobalt-fronted counter with a belt, a flatbed scanner, a card terminal and a stainless bagging well, the cashier's seat between the counter and the wall
scenes.for: conversations at the till: complaints, age checks for restricted products, card and cash payments, refusals, a queue and a customer in distress
plan: Seen from above, metres: x runs across the front of the shop from the side wall (x 0) to the right; y runs from the front cross aisle (the camera's side) toward the shopfront (y 9.0). The walls rise to 5.0 m.
Side wall (x 0): plain white-painted blockwork to the eaves. It meets the shopfront at a solid pier from x 0 to 1.5 (y 9.0), white-painted blockwork inside; the glazing starts at x 1.5.

Checkout 1 (the end one): its counter from y 1.0 (belt end) to y 5.5 (bagging end), x 1.2 to 2.0, 0.9 m high: belt from y 1.0 to 3.0, the scanner at y 3.4, the bagging well from y 4.2 to 5.5 with carrier bags on hooks at y 5.0. The cashier's pod is on the wall side: a high seat at x 1.05, y 3.6, the cash drawer under the counter, a low side panel at the pod's front end (y 4.2, 1.3 m high). The card terminal on its swivel stand at the lane edge (x 2.05, y 3.0); the customer display on its pole at the cashier's side of the counter (x 1.3, y 2.7), turned to face the lane. A staff walkway about 0.7 m wide between the pod and the wall, kept clear.
Lane 1 (x 2.0 to 3.0) runs beside it toward the shopfront. Checkout 2's counter (x 3.0 to 3.8) on the lane's other side, from y 1.0 to 5.5.
Cast: the cashier seated (head top x 1.05, y 3.6, 1.27 m); a customer standing in the lane at the scanner, facing the cashier (x 2.45, y 3.2, head top 1.68 m).

Camera: x 4.0, y 0.3 (in the front cross aisle, at the shop end of checkout 2), standing eye height 1.6 m, turned 38 degrees left of the y axis toward the side wall; 35 mm lens (55 degrees across); no tilt; horizon at 46 percent.

At the corner the solid white pier faces us (x 1396 to 1704, the glazing's sill line at y 716), then the shopfront glazing runs out of the right edge (head y about 189), the street outside soft and pale. Checkout 1 is the focal point, running from the lower left (its belt edge at x 580, y 999) toward the shopfront: the scanner at x 1025, y 810, the card terminal on its stand at x 1030, y 763, the pod's side panel at x 1035 (top y 612), the customer display at x 623 (y 575 to 704), the bagging well and its hanging bags at x 1275 to 1522 (top y about 720 to 739; bag hooks x 1417, y 681). scenes.light: Late morning, overcast. Soft grey daylight comes through the shopfront glazing at the right and ahead, so the customer's face and the right-hand faces of the counter are lit, and soft shadows fall to the left and back toward us: the bags' shadows on the stainless well, the terminal's on the counter, the counter's on the floor. The row of linear LED lights over the lane fills from above. The side wall is evenly lit, a touch warmer near the glazing. The till screen faces the cashier (its back dark); the customer display and the card terminal's small screen are on (pale lit faces, slots). No haze.
scenes.far: The shell: the side wall, the solid pier, the shopfront glazing and the street beyond, the floor and the roof above; the cashier's high seat (the cashier sits in it).
scenes.mid: Checkout 1: its counter, belt with a divider bar and a few plain items, the scanner, the pod's side panel, the till screen, the cash drawer, the card terminal and the customer display, the bagging well and the bags. scenes.what: the customer service desk at the front of the supermarket, beside the entrance: a two-height cobalt-fronted desk before a plain white wall, a bay of click and collect parcels at its end, and the automatic sliding doors with their security pedestals on the left
scenes.for: refunds and returns, complaints that escalate, click and collect handovers, lost property and a lost child, the security alarm at the exit and how to approach a customer

Right of x 3.5 the front wall is solid white-painted blockwork to x 9.5, where it meets the right side wall. A blank sign band on it from x 4.5 to 7.5, 2.6 to 3.0 m up.
Security pedestals either side of the doorway at y 9.2, x 0.3 and x 2.7 (1.6 m high).

scenes.what: the supermarket's stockroom behind the sales floor: a grey concrete floor with yellow lines, longspan shelving of plain cases, a pallet of stock on a hand pallet truck, a roll cage, a cardboard baler, and on the white back wall a fire exit and the closed goods-in roller shutter
